data: Highly recommend, for a great challenge and a great story
Incredible story, art style is amazing and the puzzles are SO fun
Highly recommend - the story is good and honestly a bit unexpected, I enjoyed the characters, and the voice acting is fantastic
Great story, great music, great gameplay
it is worth every penny as a beautiful piece of art that nonetheless holds its own as a challenging gaming experience
You will not care about any of these characters
You will not care about any of these characters
this is not for you if you're just interested in a mystery story on a ship
I don't think it's much of a spoiler to say that the primary stakes of the game are about coming to understand that story

Played this game over discord screenshare with my bruva and we had much fun. I was better than him. Screw tattoo man. Big up Martin. This game has amazingly accurate continuity but how did they get the cow in a pen with no gate???????
Anyway 9/10 just cuz of that cow thing

When I saw this game was released I bought it immediately, and I do not regret a single penny spent.
I first saw the demo through a youtube video in 2014 and loved it. I then forgot about it for 4 years and heard earlier this year it was getting released soon. Then I forgot about it again until I saw that it was released today...all I can say is that I'm never forgetting about this again.
I played for over 7 straight hours and absolutely loved it. I couldn't pull myself away from the game trying to go back and find different clues in scenes I've been in before or correcting the minor mistakes I've made with the new information I've recieved. Not only is the game intriguing, but the soundtrack is amazing!!! If you love being a detective, murder mystery, lore, 1 bit graphics, a good soundtrack, or just being on a ship, you should get this game.

Got, downloaded, and played this in it's enitrety today. Not once during that playthrough did I think to check the time. It is now well past 3 am and I regret nothing. I could go on about the reasons why this game is fantastic, but why ruin it? Get the game for yourself and go through it as blind as you can.

Return of the Obra Dinn is an excellent detective game, with an interesting and unique visual style and a great soundtrack. The game's signature flourish of incrementally confirming information you have filled in correctly keeps the game from being overwhelming and regularly provides you with those "hell yeah I am a genius" moments that keep pushing you along. I highly recommend you attempt to identify all the crew members and their fates without looking anything up. Figuring it all out, alone or with friends, is a fantastic experience. Highly recommended.

An interesting story with an interesting art style and some tricky puzzles. A very memorable experience with memorable music. Phenomenal Foley work (i.e., the sounds of the events).

This game isn't for you if you hate the art style or dislike puzzles.

But if you like puzzles, and if the odd art style and odd story telling method appeal to you, then I can't recommend this game strongly enough. This is one of those games that I wish I could play for the first time again (like Subnautica).
Really fun puzzle/murder mystery game. Fair warning it is a little hard and can be a lot at times. I recommend breaks when you feel too overwhelmed.

It genuinely angers me that this game isn't more popular.
The Paper's Please guy made a game that was (in my opinion) much better than *Paper's Please*, already a tall task, and it has an amazing soundtrack, some of my favorite moments in any game, is genuinely stellar in its design and puzzles, and is set on a pirate ship to boot.
It's such a special game with literally nothing like it, and I really wish that wasn't the case, but there's also a good shot that nothing else could be anything like it. It's simply that good.

This is a deep and engaging puzzle game not for the faint of brain (or eye). My advice, if you're thinking about playing this, avoid ANY spoilers. This is a wonderful mystery with a great art style, I just wish I could play it for the first time again. Farewell, Captain Witterel, and F you Brennan.

This game is simply brilliant. Yeah, it is strictly one-time playthrough (Ok, maybe a second one to savour the delivery once more), but that 7-10 hour have brought me more joy than tens of hours on tens oh hours of modern AAA-sandboxes.
Some professional filmmakers say sound is far more important than pictures, and Obra Dinn is a stunning champion for that idea. Music, Dialogues - curt, yet authentic, absolutely put you inside the story. It is left to a meticously built visuals - "photographs of death" - to finish off an impression. And the story, oh the story, which you kinda think you've figured out right at the start - it will show you twists, turns and sudden depths of human condition and inhuman surroundings you are not quite ready for.
Yeah, and though you can probably study XIX century maritime customs on this game, it doesn't sell "The tour edition" separately, like some projects best left unspoken of.
All in all - a unique game experience, emotional, brain-teasing, fantastic and suprisingly deep for it's undertold manner. An experience not to be missed at any gaming era.

This game is one of - if not the - greatest ever made, a stunning experience counterbalanced only by the misery I feel at never being able to experience it again with fresh eyes. Every diorama is beautifully put together, the gameplay concept is unique and brilliantly executed, and the story is compelling and, at times, haunting. After finishing it, I immediately went to find Let's Plays just so that I could attempt to relive the experience through them. It is a tragedy that this hasn't yet inspired an array of 'Obra Dinn-em-up' pretenders and sparked the development of an entire genre.

In short: 'not bad'

A brilliant deduction game, entirely deserving of the frequent praise it gets. You'll have to really think at times, that's for sure, but every mystery is solvable eventually. I will warn you though, at some point you might accidentally start doing racial profiling. I once caught myself thinking "Hm, he looks like he might have Latin features, perhaps he's that elusive Frenchman I haven't found yet".

Really really well executed idea. Make sure you can give this game the time and attention it deserves. It's not an easy win but it's satisfying to see it through. Definitely recommend this game for anyone who likes puzzles and deductive reasoning.

Early on I had a few issues with frequent crashing, but messing with some settings seemed to help. Easy to look past imo.

This game scratches a very particular mental itch. It's like an unholy fusion of Reader Rabbit meets Sudoku, where the puzzles are murder mysteries and the setting is film noir at sea.
This is the first game I've had to take physical notes for in YEARS and I am LOVING IT! You really feel like you're living this story and piecing together what happened. Normally I get frustrated with puzzle games like this and look up guides online, but there are so many little clues sprinkled throughout that the game feels like it's trying to help you! The more you pay attention, the more you're rewarded.

This was without a doubt one of the best games I've ever played. It feels like a story straight out of a book. Not only was the story engaging, but the detective element was genuinely the best I've seen. The whole concept is great, and I like the world this game takes place in, it feels like something from pirates of the caribbean with its beasts and artefacts. The first thing you would see upon boarding the Obra Dinn is the shine in the water and you'd assume its just a glare off the moon, until you reach the mermaid part of the game. The watch was very cool, I liked how it worked alot.

Is this game hard? Yes, and I love it

This is one of the best puzzle games I've ever played, its hard enough where you can always solve someone just via a little backtracking.

End of the game + someone's identity spoiler: I thought it was cool that Dr. Evans kept around a monkey, I didn't think it would serve any use other than just being his pet. That all changed in the end where Evans did this baller move with the monkey, showing that he must've used the watch before hand. That moment was probably one of my favourites in the entire game.

Would I recommend Obra Dinn? Yes!

I loved this game! I played it almost straight through in a couple days. All of the elements of the game worked well together: music, voice acting, and character graphics.
It's a fun puzzle. There were very few times when I felt really stuck but it was challenging enough throughout to keep me engaged. I highly recommend if you enjoy mystery games.

(Note: I have completed this game offline. For some reason my playtime may say 36 minutes.)

Let it be said that I'm pretty dumb, and a wonderful thing Return of the Obra Dinn does is make you feel great when you happen upon an ingenious deduction, while punishingly making you feel like a dope when you've overlooked something so incredibly obvious, you should be checked for a pulse.

This is a game I wish I could play endlessly, yet there's more than enough here to satisfy the most dogged insurance adjuster. Do yourself a favor and get this game, and for the love of god do not read any guides or hints. Everything you need is in here.
A great detective game that takes a little time to piece everything together, but very much doable on your own.

This game is amazing. From the art direction to the mystery that you uncover: Everything is done incredibly well.

My only complaint would be that you are just thrown in and don't know what details are relevant to identity the crew. This can be frustrating, but fear not, there are quite a few guides that help but don't spoil!

It took me a while to get to this game and I kept hearing how good it was but nothing prepared me for how much I actually enjoyed playing this. One of the best games I've played, a true investigation game that surprises you at every turn. Fantastic story, art style and the voice acting was amazing. I can't express enough how much I enjoyed playing this.
An well-done detective game elevated even further by a unique art style and excellent soundtrack. Great as an intro to deduction style games.

Excellent mechanics. Classic but intriguing story. Special and beautiful graphics. Amazing music.
Stunning work from the develop of Paper Please.

You play as an investigator, trying to find out what happened on Obra Dinn, an East Indian Company's ship that has set sailed and returned, with many of the shipman dead. You have a special device that can get back to the time of death of each corpse. Then you piece up the puzzles to find out what happened. You have a book that you have to mark down how each character died.

Very fun and some puzzles are just clever. I admit at a later point I was a bit clueless so I have to resort to trial and error.

If I have to be picky, I would say the ending is a lackluster. just felt ending abrupt and forced. But it doesn't hurt the whole experience.

Would recommend at full price.

*L's theme starts playing*

Not sure if I just suck or what, but some of the fates felt impossible without brute-forcing them.
Regardless, one of the best mystery/who-dunnit experiences out there, worth every second.

I'd bought this game after hearing a great deal of good things about it. The concept and the design were enough to seal the deal.

Return of the Obra Dinn was everything I'd expected- amazing, even if frustrating at times (I'm not particularly clever or observant, so much of my mystery-solving was luck-based. XD).

I don't know if there could ever be another game like this, but I sure as hell enjoyed this one. My one major complaint is WHY IS THE SOUNDTRACK NOT AVAILABLE FOR PURCHASE?

Awesome visual style, amazing storytelling, 100% totally recommend.
Completable in ~8 hours, seems harder than it is

This game is insurance claims fraud perpetrated by the East India Trading company. You take the roll of a psychotic insurance claims adjuster equipped with a 'magical' watch that sends you on delusional mind trips. I suspect the watch is actually packed with opiates but due to ESRB restrictions Lucas Pope glazes over showing you the drug use. Once aboard the Obra Dinn with your opiate watch and murder journal you reverse death note sixty souls lost tragically at sea, devising outlandish causes of death each more ludicrous than the last.

By the time you're done fantasizing about death and dismemberment you've run out of opiates and its time to head back to the mainland to send off your death note to your superior. Just don't be surprised when the letter you get back has something dead in it, after all, you assaulted him with the ravings of a madman.
best moment when the game rates a person's identity as "easy to deduce" and i have never seen this man in my life

Groaning of a weathered hull. Spectral moonbeams piercing tattered sails. The decaying remains of a doomed crew. Return of the Obra Dinn is a thoroughly enjoyable experience that presents a compelling mystery to be solved by clever mechanics and logic; revealing a tragic chronicle of greed, betrayal and violence. The unique visual style enhances the doleful essence of the narrative while being appropriately designed to facilitate and hinder your investigation. The soundtrack is also a congruous accompaniment to the dramatic scenes you witness. A spellbinding masterpiece and additional feather in the cap of Lucas Pope.

Highly recommended for every scurvy dog and lily-livered landlubber.

10/10
Very good game I like investigating boat. Uncovering everything that happened on the Obra Dinn was amazing also sound design and voice acting is GREAT.

Absolutely magnificent.

Great deductive murder mystery game.

The mystery is intriguing, and fun to solve. The aesthetic is beautiful, and the sound effects and voice acting are top notch.

It might not be for everyone, but if it grabs you, it will be a great experience.

at first i was grossed out by the fullscreen of spotty graphics. i tried again after like, an year, changed the graphics options and i LOVED IT
the only bad thing about this game is that it ends and you can play it only once. after figuring out everyone's destiny, there is literally no reason to play again bc you already know what happened to who.
anyone who plays this for the first time, DO NOT LOOK UP THE WALKTHROUGHS. If you get stuck, and i know you will at certain part, look closely at the hammocks. there are numbers on them that matches the crews number.
a few crewmates will remain in the end. it's pretty much impossible to find out what happened to them. just work on those you know for certain first, then try every possible matches until you get the remaining ones. i mean that's how i did it

i really enjoyed how the tragedy is something that already happened and you're just there to find out what fates befell on those aboard. it's not dangerous to be on the ship anymore, and we're not here to kill or save anybody, we just want to know what happened. i really hope lucas pope makes another game like this one.

as for korean players, when you play the game on korean you are likely to lose some precious clues to the translation, such as the speaker's accent. i'd recommend playing on english
The story is amazing, the art and music are outstanding. And it also made me feel very smart (I'm actually very dumb), so I'm very very happy.

One of the best detective/puzzle games I have ever played. Sometimes I felt like a genius, and then stupid again. Recommended even if you don't like puzzle games, it's not really hard. Also Soldiers of the sea ost slaps!
Its a logic puzzle. It's also very well reviewed, so unlikely that my review will make any difference, but I really just wanted to leave a thumbs up.

Never played anything like it, incredibly creative and unique. A true test of someone's deductive reasoning to the point where it was almost painful. I loved it. If you like detective games this is 100% for you.

5/5, highly recommended, wouldn't change a single thing.
Absolutely fantastic indie game. The Voice Acting, the story telling, the way it comes together. I recommend if you enjoy being a detective.

Can't believe i've never reviewed Obra Dinn. One of the finest murder mystery detective games with an ever-twisting story of mythological proportions. Lucas Pope cements himself as one of the greatest game devs.

Only downside is some of the potential methods of death sound very similar so it can be tricky to narrow down the specific wording you should be using to describe a death - ie: Speared by a monster could just as easily be Spiked by a monster. But this doesnt distract from an amazing experience.
I think this is single-handedly one of the best games I have ever played. The sound design, the voices, the style, the story, all perfect. If you have not played this, please do

This game is one of my top favourites. The story line is absolutely amazing and really well planned. The graphic style is really nice and suits the game very well.
It is a linear game so its a one time playthrough, but after several months you may forget parts and could be played again.
10/10 worth my money and time!

This game is incredibly well made, oozing with good game design and style in all possible ways.

There is attention to detail in every single corner of the massacred ship. And the details are important for you to piece together the fates of the damned. The main gripe I have against detective games is the "Choose option A or B" without any consequence, due to the great game design this isnt an issue becouse of the millions of options, making guesswork not a viable option until you have at least figured out 90% of the ship's mysteries.

The visuals might turn some off and I can see why, but personally I think it adds a lot to the style of the game. And the music is also very well made. personally one of my favorite osts. I'm definitly looking forward to Lucas Pope's next title.

The only thing that might be a slight problem is the lack of replayability, but due to the nature of the game that is unavoidable, and it doesnt take away from the overall experience you will have with this game.

I highly reccomend getting this game, as it is definitly worth its full price. I'd give it a straight up 10/10

The recent reviews don't say overwhelmingly positive for no reason.
If you like solving puzzles, anything related to pirates or interesting and creative art direction then this game is worth a shot.
It was a real pleasure piecing together the fate of crew members on the Obra Dinn.

There is very little I can say about this game that wouldn't be a spoiler, but please please PLEASE play it. I'd recommend playing with/streaming to a friend or two, if not for help with the deductions then just so more people can experience this game. It is utterly fantastic and I wish I could wipe my memory of it so I could play it all again.

It's been a couple of years since I played this game, and I still find myself thinking about it often, wishing I could play it again for the first time, and hoping the developer will make another game like this. I just want more Obra Dinn.

A truly unique and wonderful game.
The best mystery/detective game I've ever played. Lots of great puzzles, interesting mechanics, and unique art. Wish I could erase my memory and play it all over again.

I don't believe it's a stretch to call this the most innovative detective game of all time. The gameplay loop of slowly pecking away at the fates of all the crew and passengers is enthralling, frustrating, and extremely rewarding. The biggest downside to this game is it's replay potential. Unless you can have your memory wiped, you aren't going to get much from subsequent playthroughs.

Return of The Obra Dinn is a very special game that doesn't come along often. Few games push their respective genre this far forward, and I suspect we will be talking about this game for a long, long time.

9/10

Great detective/clue game with some of the most unique graphics and environment.

Recommendation: play it with a friend. They may spot details you don't or come up with alternative ways to determine identities.
Mystery game where attention to detail matters. Very enjoyable, although the graphics were definitely an... artistic choice.

Short game, but truly does tax the mind. There is a ghost ship and you are an insurance inspector that must figure out what happened to all 60 people who were on the ship's final voyage. You are privy to 'scenes' and between those, the list of the crew, and a few drawings that depict everyone, you need to use your powers of deduction to figure out what happened. Replay ability is limited, since once you solve the mystery that's about it. But it's a good story and a lot of fun if you enjoy puzzling out things.

A little difficult, but a very interesting method of story telling. I had to do a little guess and check on a couple people but it was generally solved by context clues and process of elimination and my raw deductive capabilities. The pixel style took me a little while to get use to and definitely made it harder to id some of the characters. I was intrigued and really sucked into solving this and had a lot of fun. I think the pacing on the memories is a little slow when I am excited and know and answer but am stuck in a memory waiting on the door way. I got this game a couple years ago and got stuck immediately, and now I'm SO glad I tried this game out again!

A game so good I'm waiting a few years to forget about it to replay it.
Very original and fun, just give it a bit of time at the beggining until you get what the hell is going on!
Truly, a phenomenal game. And its all pretty much a bunch of dots and lines accompanied by great cello centric music.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): players praise the story and characters most, along with the art and music.
The main complaint is that some players find the characters hard to care about.

details.text: The score has held steady lately, and only 4% of recent reviews complain about the story and characters, down from 6% of all reviews.
Players who have played only briefly are far less positive, at 63%, than those who keep going, which suggests the early hours may not win over some players.
